data.name: Selim
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Turkish word "selâm", meaning peace or security, and the Arabic word "lim", meaning moon. In Islamic tradition, Selim is the name of two sultans known for their military victories and peace treaties. In Christianity, Selim is believed to be the name of a saint who lived during the Byzantine era.

in_hebrew.name: שְׁלִים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שְׁלִים הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו אהבה ושלום, שלמות, שלוש. השם נמצא במקרא, כאשר בתהילים, פרק 85, פסוק 11, האלוהים מכונים 'שומר-שלים' (שומר השלום). בנוסף, השם 'שלים' הוא גם שם של נביא יהודי, שהוזכר בספר נחום, פרק 1, פסוק 4. השם 'שלים' נחשב לשם נוצרי, אך גם בקהילה היהודית, השם 'שלים' נחשב לשם נבון, משום שהוא מכיל את המונח 'שלום' אשר הוא חלק מברכת 'שלום-עליכם'.

in_greek.name: Σηλὴμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Σηλὴμ είναι ονομασία με ελληνική ρίζα. Η λέξη έχει την έννοια της ελπίδας, της ειρήνης και του τέλους. Ο Σηλὴμ είναι επίσης ένα ονομαστικό με ελληνική ρίζα, που εμφανίζεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη, στο βιβλίο του Ματθαίου, στη φρασική 'η ελπίς του Παναγίου' (Μαθ. 1:21) και στη φρασική 'Σηλὴμ τὸ όνομα του' (Μαθ. 1:25).

in_latin.name: Selim
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Selim significat spem, pacem, et finem. Inscriptio nominis Selim in Novo Testamento, in libro Matthaei, versu 1:21, ubi dicitur 'Spes Dei' (Spes Dei). Et in versu 1:25, ubi dicitur 'Selim nomen ejus' (Selim nomen ejus).

data.cultural_impact: The name Selim is of Middle Eastern origin and holds significant cultural importance in Turkey and the Islamic world. The name is reminiscent of the history of two great sultans - Selim I (1512-1520), who expanded the Ottoman Empire, and Selim II (1566-1574), who cemented its position as a major European power. Selim is also the name of the sixth caliph of the Sunni Islamic tradition, Selim II (1566-1574), and the name of the last Ottoman Sultan, Selim III (1757-1808), who tried to reform the Ottoman Empire.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Selim I, also known as Selim the Grim or Selim the Forceful, ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1512 to 1520. He undertook several successful military campaigns, expanding the Ottoman territories through the Balkans and the Middle East. Selim played a significant role in the decline of the Byzantine Empire and the rise of the Ottoman Empire as a major power in Europe and the Mediterranean.

Sultan Selim II, also known as Selim the Sot or Selim the Drunkard, ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1566 to 1574. He is known for his construction of the New Mosque in Istanbul and his patronage of the arts. Selim's military campaigns were less successful than those of his predecessors, leading to the loss of some Ottoman territories in the Caucasus and the Balkans.
